newsitem.title: KENYA: Power firm lifts Nairobi bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: Power firm lifts Nairobi bourse trade.

text.p: Two lots worth 13 million shillings in Kenya Power & Lighting Co lifted trading at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) on Wednesday.
The Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index closed up 5.75 points at 3028.15. Turnover rose to 19.971 million shillings on 357,825 shares from 8.150 million shillings on 224,654 share on Tuesday.
Kenya Power & Lighting Co traded 116,500 shares at a reserved price of 123 on the one-hour-hold board. That deal lifted the share on the ordinary floor to a 120 close from 115.

Brokers said there was overbidding for the power shares linked to the company's expansion projects. Kenya Power & Lighting Co is a power distribution monopoly and has recently licensed two offshore companies to generate electricity to meet a current Kenyan shortfall of more than 50 megawatts.
The two should start production by June next year.
Kenya Commercial Bank (KCB) eased to 56.50 from 58, while Barclays Bank gained a shilling to stand at 99.50 and Standard Chartered Bank rose to 46 from 45.25.
One broker said KCB shares were offloaded after the market took the view that a new primary issue that closed on Tuesday was oversubscribed.

In the issue, the government reduced its shareholding by a further 10 percent to 60 percent. Domestic investment in the bank through the Nairobi bourse is 32 percent while 8.0 percent is held by foreign portfolio investors.

"This will definitely improve its perception out there and we are likely to see the price continue to sell at a premium," the broker said, referring to more ownership of Kenya Commercial Bank passing into private hands.
Kenya Airways continued its downward trend to 9.55 from 9.70 on 127,504 shares on what traders said were worries about poor industrial relations. ($1=56 shillings)
